podcast.title: Official Breakup (1999)
podcast.body: The band officially disbanded in 1999 after vocalist and guitarist Craig Northe decided to leave, leading to the dissolution of the group. "Well yes, they officially broke up in 1999, Craig Northe, the vocalist and guitarist, had basically had enough, so he left the band and without him, everything kind of fell apart."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reunion and Name Change (2007)
podcast.body: The band reunited in 2007, initially performing as "The New Odds" because they had lost the rights to their original name, which they later regained. "At first, they were called the new odds because they lost the rights to their name to go wild to get that back."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Official House Band for Vancouver Canucks (2010)
podcast.body: In 2010, the reunited band became the official house band for the Vancouver Canucks, a professional ice hockey team. "and in 2010 became the official house band for the Vancouver Canucks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Association with Other Canadian Bands
podcast.body: The band maintained friendly relationships and camaraderie with prominent Canadian acts like The Tragically Hip and Barenaked Ladies. "and they were buddies with both the tragically hip and the bear naked ladies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Craig Northe's Songwriting Career
podcast.body: Craig Northe pursued a successful songwriting career, penning songs for various artists, including Rosanne Cash, and also composed the theme song for the popular TV show "Corner Gas." "Northe also wrote songs for a bunch of people, including Rosanne Cash, pretty good gig, and wrote the theme song to the TV show Corner Gas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive Concert Touring
podcast.body: Odds were known for their numerous concert tours throughout the 1990s. "lots of concertoers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Juno Award Nominations
podcast.body: The band received multiple nominations for Juno Awards during their active period in the 1990s, indicating critical recognition for their music. "There were a bunch of Juno nominations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Members' Post-Breakup Projects
podcast.body: Following the breakup, Craig Northe and other band members released a soul record and formed Stryper's Union with Rob Baker of The Tragically Hip, and later served as the backup band for Colin James. "Northe and a couple of other guys from the band released a soul record. They got together with Rob Baker of the tragically hip and a band called Stryper's Union, which did okay. And then they formed the backup band for Colin James for a few years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Stephen Drake's Production Career
podcast.body: Stephen Drake focused on a career as a producer and recording engineer in Vancouver, entering into a partnership with John Wozniak, known for the band Marcy Playground. "And our Stephen Drake concentrated on being a producer and recording engineer in Vancouver in partnership with John Wozniak, the guy behind the band Marcy Playground."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
